Power

Technical Directives

Directive:
 Oil Water Subsystem
Introduction

Oily waste water may contain paraffin, 
 kerosene, petrol, diesel oil, fuel oil, other oils and lubricants, this waste 
 capable of polluting surface or underground water where it has a harmful and 
 toxic effects where it forms a film interferes with the reoxygenation and 
 natural purification of surface water. So, it is why waste water has to be 
 strictly protected against the risk of contamination by meaning of water 
 separator unit to treat the waste that contains oils, fuels and solids in
 Damietta Power Station which is designed to treat 
 66 m3/h, with peaks of 168 m3/h, of waste water.

The first draft initiated by chemist; 
 Mohammed Eshra, reviewed by chemist; Aness Abo Al
 Ezz general director, revised by quality control chemist:
 Saad Sedek 
 Hasanain, 
 and accepted by eng. Mohammed Hamouda Al
 Sarag; head sector of 
 Damietta power station.

This document accepted by eng.
 Samir Abdel Gilel: EDEPC MPIS coordinator & 
 inspection and 
 quality control general director, and certified by 
 accountant Mahmoud Mohamed Soliman EDEPC admin. & financial inspection, 
 quality control general director and supervisor of inspection & quality 
 control head sector.
Information
Process Description

API Separator: In 
 this separator there are

items:
A mechanical 
 removal process of the oil particles or emulsified oil floating on the 
 surface.

A 
 sedimentation process of the solids by coagulation of fine suspended 
 matter with formation of sludge, which is 
 discharged to the clarifier sludge collection sump for water /sludge 
 separation.

sections.text: Induced Air Floatation

items:
It is mainly used to remove the residual oil 
 and solids still present in the waste after the pretreatment process in the 
 API Separator.

The separation process takes place in a unit 
 provided with four equal cells in series.

sections.text: Flow Description

items:
The oil contaminated waste water
 coming from the drains of Modules 1, 2 and 3 gas 
 and steam turbine areas and fuel oil treatment skids area is collected 
 in the three steam turbine sump basins and from these sumps 
 delivered to the API Separator through the pumps 1,2,3 LG-P-22A/B.

According to the waste water flow measured by the 
 flow transmitter FT-09 the two flow controllers FC09 A/B will regulate the 
 dosing of Alum and coagulant aid to 
 be delivered into the API Separator 
 by the dedicated pumps of the Chemical Feed 
 Subsystem.

The required plant supply usually ranges 
 from 23 to 66 m3/h with peaks of 
 130 m3/h and eventual maximum peaks of 168 m3/h.

sections.text: Second Stage of the Treatment

It is effected in the Induced Air 
 Flotation unit Z-04, which has the function to remove the residual oil up 
 to 10 ppm after the first stage.
 This unit can handle sudden maximum flows 
 of 168 m3/h for 15 minutes. The pretreated waste water is 
 delivered from the API Separator to the Induced Air 
 Flotation unit by the water separator transfer pumps p-25 A/B. A/B.
 The pretreated waste water with added 
 coagulant aid enters the unit from the inlet compartment and 
 then goes through the four cells in series.
 The liquid in each cell is circulated
 through the agitator 
 impeller Z-04B (C) (D) (E) two or three times 
 before passing to the next cell ( when running at rated flow 
 rate with a four minutes residence time).

The impeller located in the central zone of each cell
 rotates creating a vortex and a negative pressure which drains air 
 (gas) down the stand pipe in the top 
 center area entraining it in the liquid and forcing the air rich liquid 
 through out lateral zones of the cell.

The conical shroud of the agitator and 
 vanes redirect the motion of this two phase liquid in a radial
 pattern. This insures even distribution to all 
 parts of the cell and prevents a circular flow pattern from being 
 established on the lateral surfaces of the cell which would tend to draw 
 the oil and / or solids to the center of the cell instead of moving them 
 to the edges of the cell where they can be skimmed.

Once the two phase 
 liquid enters the lateral zone of the cell the air is released as finely 
 disseminated bubbles.

Under proper 
 conditions, usually imposed by the addition of a polyelectrolyte, 
 the contaminating oils and / or solids adhere to the bubbles.

As the bubbles
 are entrained they have a potential 
 energy which would normally be 
 released by expanding as they rise to the surface.

The theory behind this type of flotation 
 is to contact the bubbles in their high 
 potential energy stage with the contaminates in order that they can 
 give up their potential energy in adhering to the contaminating 
 particles.

This contact takes place in the mixing and 
 flotation zones. The polyelectrolyte
 changes the charges of the particles and 
 further enhances and promotes this adherence.

It is necessary to make sure all the 
 liquid entering the unit has the maximum 
 exposure to flotation zone, this accomplished by the recirculation 
 pattern and by the still well which provides a "sweeping" action across 
 the bottom of the cell which is important because the liquid passes under 
 the baffles which divide each of the compartments.

It has been calculated that the liquid in 
 each cell is circulated two to three times through the contact and 
 flotation zones before passing to the 
 next cell (when running at rated flow rate with four minutes residence 
 time ).
 Since the four cells are running in series, 
 the contaminants have 8 to 12 opportunities to be contacted with the air 
 (gas) bubbles.

As previously 
 mentioned, 
 flow through the unit is under flow, each cell being separated by a 
 baffle which is open at the bottom. The baffle 
 also extends out of the liquid to the top of the tank interior.
 This prevents the oil and / or solids 
 from migrating from one cell to the next.

Each cell removes 75% 
 of the contaminants which enter that cell and therefore
 each cell is progressively cleaner than the 
 previous cell. From the outlet compartment of unit Z-04 the clean waste 
 water is discharged to the Lined Pond Basin.
Third Stage of the Treatment

It's water/oil separation consists in separating the residual water from 
 oil.

This stage is manually performed, when the H.L. alarm is operated in the 
 Waste Oil Reservoir, discharging the separated water with the help of the 
 sample valves located along the vertical side of the vessel.

When the 
 vessel is full of oil, this can be manually transferred to disposal or by 
 means of pump P-26. The possibility of recovered oil recirculation to API 
 Separator is provided through pump P-26.
Unit Description
API Separator

The API 
 Separator is a large concrete made basin
 where the first stage of water 
 /oil separation takes place.

It is 
 designed for a peak flow of 168 m3/h with 
 retention time of 0.4 hour.

The API 
 Separator includes the following equipment.
 - Two 100 % sludge pumps p-24 A/B
 - One chain rake Z-03.
 - One oil skimmer.
 - Two 100 % recirculation pumps p-25 A/B.

sections.text:
Protective 
Maintenance
Routine Chemical Test

There are many tests carried out on the water 
 produce from the API Separator and from the final treatment of the unit to 
 obtain high quality water. These tests are
pH Value

The pH is measured in the final discharge 
 basin and in chemical lab. using pH meters designed for this purpose. The 
 suitable pH value for coagulation process was found to be (6-9).
Turbidity Value

The turbidity is measured by using Turb 550 
 (WTW). Turbidimeters to keep it in permissible limits.
Total Suspended Solids

The total suspended solid is measured by 
 using an ashless filter paper, previously dried at 105 oC and 
 weighed. Dry at 105oC for about 2 hours until the weight is 
 constant, then determine ( T.S.S ), the range of T.S.S is 10 ppm.
The Oil Test

The oil is determined in the chemical lab. 
 using separating funnel and chemical reagents for extraction of oil from 
 water (petroleium ether).
Maintenance of API Separator Chain Rake
Routine Checks

With the rake running carry out and record 
 on the proper form the following checks and tests: 
 a) Vibration b) Bearing temperature

sections.text:
Maintenance 
Instructions for Quadricell Flotation Separator
Lubrication

items:
Mechanism bearings: 
 lubricate every 3000 hours with grease N. 2 ( AGIP GRMU-EP2, IP ATESIA 
 CR2, or equivalent). First filling = 0.31 kg. each. Consumption =
 ~ 4 gm./100h each or the 8 bearings

Skimmer gearmotors: replace oil every 3000 hours, oil 
 viscosity 33.5 E at 50C (AGIP BLASIA 
 450, IP MELLANA 460, or equivalent). First filling = 0.6 I each. 
 Consumption = 0.005 1/100 h each of the 2 gearmotors. Check oil level 
 every 50 days

Skimmer bearings: grease 
 with a high grade silicon grease every 3000 hours. First filling = 50 gm. 
 each. 
 Consumption = ~ 1.5 gm./100 h each of the bearings.

Electric motors : lubricate per manufacturer 
 standard.

Skimmer blades: adjust for clearance between blades 
 and level bars from 1mm. to 3 mm. as bearing wear.
Nuts and bolts: check for tightness every 30 days.

sections.text: API Separator Sludge Sump Pumps
Routine Checks

With the units running carry out and record 
 on the proper form the following checks and tests: 
 a) Vibration. b) Bearing temperature. c) Electric motor current and 
 voltage.

d) Speed. 
 e) Delivery pressure. f) 
 Water flow rate.
Preventive Maintenance ( Isolation Procedure )

When servicing has to be carried out be 
 sure that:

items:
The delivery valve V-033A( B) 
 is in closed position.

Vent and drain valves are in 
 open position.

The electric motor breaker is 
 racked out from the power supply board.

The work permit is duly 
 filledin according to the currently in force safety clearance 
 procedure,
 signed by operating personnel and complete with a sketch showing, at 
 least, the following:
 - 
 Valves position (close or open). 
 - Blanketings to be installed.
